title: The Reflection-Principle Form of the Ballot Number, BN(a,b) = C(a+b,b) − C(a+b,b−1)

problemStatement.plain: The ballot number BN(a,b) counts sequences of a up-steps and b down-steps whose every partial sum stays strictly positive. The parent entry defines it as C(a+b-1,a-1) - C(a+b-1,a); this problem proves the alternative reflection-principle form C(a+b,b) - C(a+b,b-1) (André's derivation) and reconciles the two derivations of the ballot number in a single Lean file.
whyMatters: The ballot number has two famous elementary derivations — the Dvoretzky–Motzkin cycle lemma and André's reflection principle — that produce different-looking closed forms; reconciling them is exactly showing the two derivations agree.

Formalizing the equality turns combinatorial folklore into a machine-checked binomial identity and completes the arithmetic layer of the ballot family alongside the parent's probability and Catalan corollaries.
It exercises the pure binomial-shift API (Pascal's rule and symmetry C(n,k) = C(n,n-k)) that recurs throughout the ballot/Catalan strand.

open: The equality C(a+b-1,a-1) - C(a+b-1,a) = C(a+b,b) - C(a+b,b-1) has not been formalized in this repository.
The reflection-principle derivation and the cycle-lemma derivation of the ballot number have not been reconciled in a single Lean file.
knownResults.goal: Prove ballotNumber a b = C(a+b,b) - C(a+b,b-1) for a ≥ 1 (as a truncated natural-number identity), reusing the parent's ballotNumber definition, and assemble the reflection form together with the existing cycle-lemma/aggregate results so both derivations of BN(a,b) live in one file.
